stories.title: AI and a human mathematician both claim Riemann Hypothesis proofs
stories.summary: Mathematicians are examining two independent, nearly simultaneous claims on the Riemann Hypothesis: one produced with AI, and one a fully human proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis by Alessandro Masullo, reviewed by Brian Conrad.
stories.more: One claim comes from an AI system, which TechCrunch says has left mathematicians stunned by the result on the 167-year-old conjecture. The other is a human-only proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis by Alessandro Masullo, which Stanford's Brian Conrad has spent months reviewing, incorporating feedback, and says is looking good, according to a note from Ravi Vakil quoted by Simon Willison. The original plan was to bring Masullo to Stanford for a year to refine the writing before announcing the proof more widely, though it's unclear from available excerpts whether that timeline still holds. Latent Space's AI News roundup also flagged the Riemann Hypothesis as proved "twice independently" in the same news cycle. Full verification of either claim is not yet available.

items.excerpt: Mathematicians are having their minds blown by the latest AI-driven result — and there's a competing human solution, too.

items.title: Quoting Ravi Vakil
items.excerpt: Alessandro Masullo has a proposed proof of [Generalized Riemann Hypothesis], and Brian Conrad has been looking closely at it for months and gave extensive feedback which is being incorporated, and it is so far looking good. It is all human, with no AI. The hope was to bring Alessandro to Stanford for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people. Now it seems best to put out the current draft. — Ravi Vakil , Hurried Announcement: Alessandro Masullo GRH Tags:

Ars Technica describes the resulting privacy exposure as happening "at an alarming rate." The report frames this as evidence of a systemically leaky AI supply chain rather than an isolated incident. The report finds some AI capabilities keep improving along an exponential trajectory, consistent with earlier versions of the graph. However, it also finds that models are not as strong on tasks requiring judgment as they are on coding tasks. The report does not specify which models were evaluated or the exact size of the gap between coding and judgment-based time horizons in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Paper proposes Posterior Matching Distillation for diffusion models
stories.summary: A new paper introduces Posterior Matching Distillation, a technique to compress diffusion image and video generators into few-step students while avoiding the diversity loss of reverse-KL-based distillation.
stories.more: Diffusion distillation speeds up image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher model's many-step sampling process into a student that needs far fewer network evaluations. Existing distribution-matching approaches typically rely on reverse-KL objectives, which the paper says have a mode-seeking bias that favors a teacher's dominant outputs at the expense of sample diversity. Posterior Matching Distillation is presented as a new member of this distribution-matching family, designed to address that diversity loss. The paper was published to Hugging Face's Daily Papers listing; further benchmark results and comparisons are not included in the available excerpt.

items.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
items.excerpt: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. stories.title: OpenAI cuts reasoning-extraction attack success rate from 54% to 0.2%
stories.summary: OpenAI strengthened safeguards on GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol against attacks that extract their internal reasoning, cutting the adaptive red-team success rate from 54% to 0.2%, and suspends thousands of accounts weekly over distillation.
stories.more: The Decoder reports that OpenAI significantly strengthened protections against attackers extracting the internal reasoning of its GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol models. In adaptive red-teaming tests, the success rate for extracting that protected reasoning fell from 54 percent to 0.2 percent. OpenAI is also suspending thousands to tens of thousands of accounts each week over what it describes as coordinated distillation campaigns. Technical details of the new safeguards and how the red-teaming tests were conducted are not given in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Signal blocks screenshots on iOS and Android to stop AI agents reading chats
stories.summary: Signal is blocking screenshots on iOS 27 and Android to prevent AI agents like Siri, Gemini, and Meta's Muse from reading private chats, calling the agents an "existential threat" to privacy.
stories.more: The Decoder reports that Signal's screenshot-blocking move targets AI agents including Apple's Siri AI, Google's Gemini Intelligence, and Meta's Muse, which could otherwise read private chat content on-screen. Signal calls these AI agents an "existential threat" to privacy. The company acknowledges its protections remain incomplete, including on macOS. Signal is calling on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to adopt similar protections.

The comments come as various US states and cities move to restrict or add conditions to new data center applications. It is unclear how such a tax would be implemented or whether it has legislative backing so far.

stories.title: Nvidia board cited Jensen Huang's "lack of candor" before his resignation
stories.summary: Wired reports Nvidia's board was alarmed less by allegations of Jensen Huang's multiple affairs, including with a direct report and an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, than by his "lack of candor," ahead of his resignation.
stories.more: According to sources cited by Wired, Nvidia's board faced allegations that former CEO Jensen Huang had multiple affairs, including with a direct report and someone alleged to be a Chinese intelligence asset. Despite the seriousness of those allegations, Wired's sources say the board's primary concern was Huang's "lack of candor" rather than the conduct itself. The report ties these events to Huang's resignation as CEO. Further details on the timeline, the board's decision-making process, and corroboration of the intelligence-asset allegation are not given in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Report: financing, not survival, is the challenge for space-based AI chips
stories.summary: TechCrunch examines how chips can be engineered to survive the space environment, but lenders are wary of financing hardware that could be shot into orbit, raising questions for space-based data centers.
stories.more: The piece frames the technical challenge of space data centers as largely solved: chips can be engineered to survive the space environment. The harder problem, per TechCrunch, is financing, since lenders are reluctant to treat orbital hardware as recoverable collateral, an issue illustrated by concerns about SpaceX launches. The report frames this as a broader open question for the emerging category of space-based data centers. Specific lenders, deal terms, or companies currently pursuing orbital data centers are not named in the available excerpt.
